To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the coordinate rings of the type-A GIT quotients of the variety of complete flags are generated in degrees strictly less than the dimension of the variety, and (2) the Gelfand–Zetlin semigroups of type A are generated in degree exponential in the size of the semigroup.

the weight ring of type A is generated by elements whose degrees are bounded from above by the Krull dimension (which is O(n2)), and that the associated Gelfand– Tsetlin semigroup can have essential elements of degree exponential in n.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of weight rings in type A, and their associated semigroups of Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns.
the study of the algebraic structure of the weight rings of type-A quiver varieties.
the structure of the coordinate rings of certain GIT quotients of the flag varieties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the degree bounds for weight rings and Gelfand– Tsetlin semigroup are very different, but we do not have such a statement yet.
the weight ring is generated by elements in degrees strictly less than the dimension, and that the semigroup of GTPs has an essential generator of exponential degree.
the weight ring is generated by elements with degree polynomial in n, while the associated semigroup has generators with degree exponential in n.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the semigroups are much more complicated than the rings.
the weight rings in type A are much more tractable than their semigroups, and the latter are in general not well-behaved in terms of generators and degrees.
the weight rings are much nicer than their associated Gelfand– Tsetlin semigroup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gelfand– Tsetlin semigroup can be viewed as a semigroup of operators on the weight ring, which is a module over the semigroup.
the semigroup structure of a weight ring is much simpler than its ring structure.
the degree bounds in the two problems are not related.
